name: WHMCS
subcategory: billing and client automation for hosts
tagline: Self-hosted billing, provisioning and support platform for web hosting and domain resellers.

pricing.basis: monthly license tiered by client count
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: If you resell hosting to a dozen clients, the part of WHMCS you actually touch is small: recurring invoices, a card on file, an account created on the server when payment clears, and an email when it fails. That is a weekend build with Stripe plus the WHM API, and it will feel faster than WHMCS because it does one-tenth as much. The gap opens the moment you sell domains, because registrar automation means EPP codes, transfer states, renewal windows and a different API per registrar, none of which you want to own. Add tax rules, dunning, proration on upgrades, a client portal and a ticket system and you are rebuilding a product, not a script. Verdict: fine for your own small book of clients, bad idea for a business you want to grow.
coreLoopDIY: Bills a small client list on recurring Stripe subscriptions and provisions or suspends their cPanel accounts automatically based on payment status.
requirements: WHM/cPanel API token on your server (or another provisioning target)
SMTP or a transactional email API key
A small always-on server to host it
whatYouLose: Domain registrar automation: registrations, transfers, EPP codes, renewal windows, per-registrar APIs
Dozens of pre-built payment gateway modules, plus fraud checks and dunning workflows that already work
The addon and module ecosystem, where someone else has already built your weird edge case
Tax and invoice compliance across jurisdictions: VAT rules, sequential invoice numbering, credit notes
A polished client portal with tickets, upgrades, proration and self-service everything
moatNotes: The license fee mostly buys the long tail: registrars, gateways, control panels and third-party modules you would otherwise maintain yourself.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because hosting is a low-margin business where the billing system has to be boring and correct, and WHMCS has spent years absorbing the ugly details: a registrar changing its API, a gateway adding 3DS, a tax rule changing in one country, a client who wants to downgrade mid-cycle. A solo reseller can skip all of that with a script. Anyone with real clients and real revenue finds that the license costs less than one weekend a quarter of maintenance, and the module ecosystem means someone else already solved the thing they need next week.
notes: Great for the guy reselling hosting to his five freelance clients, bad for anyone who wants to sell domains.
prompt:
Build a minimal self-hosted hosting billing and provisioning app for a single admin (me) managing a small list of clients.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, schema created on boot with plain SQL migrations in /db
- Stripe for subscriptions and Checkout, webhooks for payment events
- Nodemailer over SMTP for email
- Single admin login: one bcrypt password hash in .env, cookie session, no user table

Data model: clients (name, email, stripe_customer_id, status), services (client_id, plan, price, cpanel_username, domain, stripe_subscription_id, status), invoices mirrored from Stripe (id, client_id, amount, status, hosted_url), events (append-only audit log of every provisioning action).

Features in scope:
1. Admin dashboard: list clients, services, and the last 50 events.
2. Create a client, create a Stripe customer, generate a Stripe Checkout link for a chosen plan, email it.
3. Webhook handler for checkout.session.completed, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.deleted.
4. Provisioning adapter at /lib/provision.ts with createAccount, suspendAccount, unsuspendAccount, terminateAccount. Implement one real adapter against the cPanel WHM JSON API using WHM_HOST and WHM_API_TOKEN, plus a FakeAdapter used when PROVISION_DRIVER=fake.
5. On first successful payment, create the cPanel account and email credentials. On payment_failed, wait 7 days (a cron route hit by an external scheduler), then suspend. On subscription deleted, suspend immediately and never auto-terminate.
6. Read-only client page at /c/[token] showing services, status, invoice links and a Stripe billing portal link.

Explicitly out of scope: domain registrar APIs, tax and VAT calculation, ticket system, multi-currency, proration logic, affiliate program, plugin system, multi-admin roles.

All secrets in .env (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, WHM_HOST, WHM_API_TOKEN, SMTP_URL, ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH, APP_URL). No telemetry, no analytics, no external services beyond Stripe, SMTP and the WHM host. Include a README with setup steps, how to add a plan, and how to point a cron service at the dunning route.
